summary.headline: JSW Energy Q2 FY27: revenue up 24% YoY to ₹6,658 crore and PAT attributable up 50% to ₹1,056 crore, with 1.4 GW commissioned since April.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 24% YoY to ₹6,658 crore and EBITDA rose 23% to ₹3,907 crore, with net generation up 17% to 17.5 BU. Installed capacity crossed 15.1 GW after 513 MW of Q2 additions and the 300 MW Maruti Clean Coal acquisition (closed 6 August). Merchant realisation of ~₹6.9/unit was about 20% above the DAM average of ₹5.7/unit, supported by bilateral contracts. Management reaffirmed 2.5–3 GW annual RE additions and a 30 GW target for 2030, and said the Q3 merchant book is fully booked at similar or better prices.

financial_highlights.change: down ~51 bps from 8.79% a year ago

financial_highlights.metric: Net debt / TTM EBITDA (excluding CWIP debt)

segments.name: Thermal
segments.commentary: Consolidated thermal PLF 75% vs All-India 67.8%; generation 8.9 BU up 13% YoY including 321 MU from Maruti. Mahanadi ran at 90% PLF; Utkal at 82% PLF with plant EBITDA up over 3x YoY to ₹368 crore.

segments.name: Hydro
segments.commentary: Hydro generation 3,421 MU, up 13% YoY, against a national decline of ~15%. Kutehr generated ~408 MU at ~78% PLF; Tidong (commissioned Q1 FY27) generated 199 MU at 61% PLF; Karcham Wangtoo and Baspa at ~90% consolidated PLF.

segments.name: Renewables (wind and solar)
segments.commentary: Wind PLF 46% and solar PLF 19%; generation up 25% for wind and 36% for solar on ~1.5 GW YoY capacity increase. Q2 additions were 301 MW solar and 212 MW hybrid.

guidance_outlook: FY27 organic RE commissioning target of 3 GW (1.4 GW done since April, 1.6 GW remaining and described as fully on track); management says the 2.5–3 GW annual pace will hold each year.
FY27 capex about ₹20,000 crore; cash accrual about ₹6,500 crore plus ~₹7,150 crore equity from fundraising and JSW Steel share monetisation.
Operational capacity expected at about 16.7–16.8 GW by year-end FY27; 1 GWh of standalone BESS to be commissioned in FY27 (Rajasthan and Kerala, under ESAs).
KSK Mahanadi 1,200 MW expansion: 600 MW unit by FY28 and balance 1,200 MW by FY29; capex per MW guided at least 25–30% below industry average.
Salboni 3,200 MW (four 800 MW units): first unit expected by 2030; boilers ordered from the Durgapur facility.
Interest-rate sensitivity: management assumes ~30 bps increase in average cost of debt (to ~8.5%) if a further 75 bps rate hike occurs; new projects underwritten at 9% cost of debt over 25 years.
Q3 FY27 merchant volumes fully booked at similar or better than ₹6.9/unit; Q4 discussions under way.
Maruti Clean Coal acquisition: EV ₹1,410 crore, EBITDA and PAT accretive from day one; ₹45 crore EBITDA in 55 days of ownership.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity above 15.1 GW after 1.7 GW added since April (1.4 GW organic plus 300 MW Maruti); renewables about 61% of portfolio.
Locked-in pipeline toward 30 GW by 2030; 4 capacity categories beyond 2030 cited: C&I, group captive, pumped hydro (~26.4 GWh pipeline) and thermal.
C&I installed portfolio incl. group captive 3.7 GW (~25% of operating capacity), targeted at over 8.5 GW by 2030.
Halol wind blade facility producing since June; Chitradurga facility on track for completion in Q3 FY27.
Toshiba JSW stake raised to 10.7% in July; GE Power India boiler business acquisition received NCLT sanction on 1 October, closing expected soon.
Punatsangchhu-III (920 MW, Bhutan): DPR stage; project cost and timeline to be shared after details due by June 2027.
demand_pricing: Power demand grew ~11.1% YoY in Q2 FY27 (September +11.3%); October month-to-date growth 21.2%; peak demand touched 270 GW; monsoon ~13% below normal.
DAM prices averaged ₹5.7/unit in Q2; JSW merchant realisation ~₹6.9/unit (about 20% above DAM). Merchant volume 1.1 BU, about 7% of energy sold and about 4% of capacity (all thermal).
API4 imported coal averaged ~US$115/t in Q2, up ~28% YoY; company says domestic coal shift and job-work arrangements at imported-coal plants shielded it from the increase.

Curtailment was ~4.8% of generation in H1 vs national ~5.4%; Q2 curtailed ~225 MU with ~₹59 crore revenue impact. About 60% of curtailed capacity on temporary GNA to move to permanent GNA by end-Q3 FY27.
Group RTC demand expected to more than double to ~7 GW by 2032; 4.5 GW of 6.2 GW Group MoUs yet to be tied up, with 2 GW under advanced discussion.

qa_highlights.question: Are the Mahanadi expansion PPAs utility-type, given Chhattisgarh discom rules requiring in-state capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said new discom PPAs are expected, with the 5% free-power commitment to Chhattisgarh as the existing obligation. A part of the capacity may be kept for short-term merchant sale given low fuel cost near the mine; first unit FY28, balance two in FY29.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sharp QoQ jump in Utkal EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 had outages and lower availability, limiting merchant sales; Q2 PLF was ~82% with long-term PPAs with Karnataka and Assam, and better merchant sales added to fixed-cost recovery.

qa_highlights.question: Tenure of the 25% fixed-rate debt?
qa_highlights.answer: About 15% is forex-linked and fully hedged for rates and FX, with tenor ~5–6 years; the rest is NCDs with ~4–5 years tenor.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 1 GWh BESS linked to PPA capacity or merchant?
qa_highlights.answer: All BESS in FY27 is under ESAs in Rajasthan and Kerala; these are standalone BESS with no solar investment. Separately, solar-plus-battery for evening-peak sales is planned, with evening connectivity applied about 8 months earlier.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 30 GW target fully PPA-backed, and what IRR threshold applies to group captive deals?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 30 GW plan contains only ~800 MW of Salboni Phase I, with the other ~2.4 GW beyond 2030; all under-construction RE is under PPA, including 2 GW of group captive under discussion. Minimum benchmark is mid-to-high-teen IRR.

qa_highlights.question: Is KSK 1,200 MW commissioning by FY29 realistic?
qa_highlights.answer: Equipment is already ordered, and balance-of-plant, coal and ash handling, rail and transmission for 3.6 GW are in place, so a ~3-year timeline is expected versus 4.5–5 years for greenfield.

qa_highlights.question: What is the interest-rate impact if rates rise 75 bps?
qa_highlights.answer: Only ~75% of the floating book is MCLR-linked; management assumes ~40 bps pass-through and ~30 bps effective increase, taking cost of debt to ≤8.5%. No impact on the 9%-underwritten new projects.

qa_highlights.question: Run-rate EBITDA and FY27 net debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not share run-rate EBITDA or forward guidance; it indicated a 16.7–16.8 GW base by year-end. FY27 equity funding visibility is ~₹13,150 crore (₹6,500 crore accruals plus ₹7,150 crore fundraising and share monetisation).

risks_watch: Interest-rate exposure: ~75% of term debt is floating, mostly MCLR-linked; management guides to ≤8.5% cost of debt in a further hike scenario.
Curtailment in Gujarat and Rajasthan corridor; ~225 MU lost in Q2 (₹59 crore). Permanent GNA for ~60% of the affected capacity due by end-Q3 FY27.
Merchant pricing sustainability: Q3 is booked at ~₹6.9/unit or better; Q4 still under negotiation. Evening-peak BESS economics depend on continued peak price spreads.
Execution: 1.6 GW of remaining FY27 RE additions; KSK 1,200 MW expansion by FY29; Salboni Phase I first unit by 2030.
Imported coal price pressure (API4 ~US$115/t, up ~28% YoY); company relies on domestic coal and job-work arrangements to offset.
Management declined to disclose run-rate EBITDA, and an analyst requested economics disclosure for new RE projects; watch for any change in disclosure.
summary.management_tone: Confident and forward-leaning on demand, firm-power and capacity delivery, with several explicit reaffirmations of targets. More guarded on forward numbers: declined to give run-rate EBITDA, Bhutan project cost (awaiting June 2027 DPR) or merchant pricing beyond Q3, and deflected the Chhattisgarh PPA question toward "we will take a call at the right time."
key_quotes: The pipeline is substantially de-risked, and we are confident of achieving our 3 GW commissioning target for FY27, supported by planned capex of around ₹20,000 crore.
Yes, definitely, the project work has started, as we have said that the first unit is expected to be commissioned in FY28 and balance two Units in FY29.
Sharad Mahendra: Yes. Definitely, third quarter is fully booked.
Run rate EBITDA, I think normally, we don't share that information.
So we will take a call at the right time, but we are confident that selling this capacity will not be a problem because of the low fuel cost being close to the mine.

growth.why: Management reaffirmed FY27 guidance of 3 GW RE commissioning (1.4 GW done, 1.6 GW remaining, on track) with ~₹20,000 crore capex, year-end operational capacity of 16.7–16.8 GW, and 2.5–3 GW annual additions thereafter; Q3 merchant volumes are fully booked, but the 1.6 GW remaining and the KSK expansion have specific timing while the pricing and demand support is only partly quantified.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 merchant realisation ~₹6.9/unit was ~20% above DAM ₹5.7/unit, Q3 merchant book fully booked at similar or better prices, and 16.7-16.8 GW run-rate base by year-end should add fixed-cost recovery; but Q4 pricing is still under negotiation and API4 coal is up ~28% YoY to ~US$115/t.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 1.4 GW already commissioned since April with 1.6 GW of the 3 GW FY27 RE target remaining and described as fully on track, taking operational capacity to ~16.7-16.8 GW by year-end FY27; ~₹20,000 crore FY27 capex is committed.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Net generation up 17% YoY to 17.5 BU, renewables generation up 25% (wind) and 36% (solar) on ~1.5 GW added, and power demand growing ~11% in Q2 with October month-to-date at 21.2%; curtailment of ~4.8% of generation is a drag until permanent GNA for ~60% of affected capacity by end-Q3 FY27.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is 75% for consolidated thermal (vs All-India 67.8%) and the 2.5-3 GW annual RE pace, KSK Mahanadi 1,200 MW expansion (600 MW by FY28) and Salboni 3,200 MW are already planned, with the 30 GW 2030 target and ~2.4 GW beyond 2030 needing further sanctions; FY27 equity visibility is ~₹13,150 crore.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management reaffirmed the 3 GW FY27 target and 2.5-3 GW annual pace but declined to give run-rate EBITDA or forward numbers; Q3 merchant book is fully booked at ~₹6.9/unit or better, which could support a raise if Q4 pricing holds.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Risks include 1.6 GW of remaining FY27 RE execution, ~225 MU Q2 curtailment (₹59 crore), imported coal at ~US$115/t (+28% YoY), and ~75% floating-rate debt where a further 75 bps hike lifts cost of debt to ~8.5% from 8.28%.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: 1 GWh standalone BESS in Rajasthan and Kerala to be commissioned in FY27 under ESAs, Halol wind blade facility already producing since June, Chitradurga facility due Q3 FY27, and solar-plus-battery for evening-peak sales planned.

rows.label: Group RTC/captive demand and MoU conversion
rows.why: 4.5 GW of 6.2 GW Group MoUs not yet tied up with 2 GW under advanced discussion, and group RTC demand expected to reach ~7 GW by 2032.

rows.label: Permanent GNA for curtailed capacity
rows.why: About 60% of curtailed capacity moves from temporary to permanent GNA by end-Q3 FY27, which should cut the ~225 MU Q2 curtailment (₹59 crore) loss.

rows.label: Net debt/EBITDA falling below 5x
rows.why: Net debt/TTM EBITDA is ~4.94x, down from ~5.2x in FY26, and cost of debt fell 51 bps YoY to 8.28%, though the rate-hike sensitivity could reverse part of this.

tone.note: Management was confident on the 3 GW FY27 RE target, 2.5-3 GW annual pace, and Q3 merchant booking, but guarded on run-rate EBITDA, Bhutan project cost, and merchant pricing beyond Q3; analysts pressed on Chhattisgarh in-state PPA rules and RE project economics.
